headline: AI prompts you to write, fighting writer's block and AI detection
summary: A new 'prompt-me' skill uses AI to generate prompts for human writers, aiming to overcome creative blocks and the uncanny feeling of AI-generated text.
details: Tired of AI writing most of your content, leaving you with a sense of remorse? This new 'prompt-me' skill offers a solution by having AI prompt the human writer, rather than the other way around.
The goal is to overcome writer's block and the uncanny feeling of AI-generated text. Instead of AI doing the bulk of the writing, it helps structure the human's creative process.
This approach is also presented as a more ethical alternative to using AI detection evasion techniques, which can involve instructing AI to mimic human writing patterns.
Inspired by tools like Matt Pocock's 'grill-me' skill, 'prompt-me' focuses on creative writing by generating a series of prompts for the user to respond to.

The developer notes that while 'prompt-me' shares a similar concept with 'grill-me', it's distinct in its application to creative writing and aims to keep the majority of the actual writing with the human.
The 'prompt-me' skill is available on GitHub, with the developer planning to test its effectiveness and potentially refine its size and functionality.
caption:
Feeling like AI is doing all the writing? A new tool flips the script, using AI to prompt YOU to write, fighting writer's block and the uncanny valley of AI prose.

Tired of AI writing most of your content, leaving you with a sense of remorse? This new 'prompt-me' skill offers a solution by having AI prompt the human writer, rather than the other way around.

The goal is to overcome writer's block and the uncanny feeling of AI-generated text. Instead of AI doing the bulk of the writing, it helps structure the human's creative process.

This approach is also presented as a more ethical alternative to using AI detection evasion techniques, which can involve instructing AI to mimic human writing patterns.

Inspired by tools like Matt Pocock's 'grill-me' skill, 'prompt-me' focuses on creative writing by generating a series of prompts for the user to respond to.

The developer notes that while 'prompt-me' shares a similar concept with 'grill-me', it's distinct in its application to creative writing and aims to keep the majority of the actual writing with the human.

The 'prompt-me' skill is available on GitHub, with the developer planning to test its effectiveness and potentially refine its size and functionality.

headline_marked: [[Switzerland's Federal Government]] Ditches Microsoft 365 for Open Source
headline: Switzerland's Federal Government Ditches Microsoft 365 for Open Source
summary: A pilot program will replace Microsoft 365 with open-source alternatives on 3,000 workstations, aiming for full migration by 2027.
details: Switzerland's federal government is embarking on a significant shift, launching a pilot program to replace Microsoft 365 with open-source alternatives across 3,000 workstations. This initiative represents approximately 7% of the federal workforce, with a target completion date set for the end of 2027.

The move is driven by a new digital sovereignty law and follows a successful proof-of-concept, 'PoC BOSS', which involved 172 federal employees testing the openDesk suite. While core office tasks received positive feedback, large-scale video conferencing still presented technical limitations.

The Federal Chancellery is investing CHF 9 million into this open-source workplace rollout. The pilot phase will see the new system running in parallel with Microsoft 365, allowing for a gradual transition rather than an abrupt switch, which is crucial for such a large-scale migration.

This migration addresses key concerns: the risk of foreign access to sensitive Swiss government data due to US cloud legislation, the operational risk of depending on a single foreign vendor, and escalating costs associated with proprietary licensing fees.

Switzerland's military cybersecurity unit, Cyber Command, is moving even faster, set to replace Microsoft 365 entirely with openDesk by October 2026, citing similar concerns about foreign access to sensitive data.

The EMBAG Law, effective since 2024, mandates that all Swiss federal agencies publish government-developed software as open source by default, promoting digital sovereignty and fostering innovation. This aligns with the Federal Council's designation of digital sovereignty as a primary focus theme for December 2025.

Neighboring countries like France and Germany are also exploring similar transitions away from major tech providers. The success of this Swiss initiative could set a precedent for other nations seeking greater digital independence.

In response, Microsoft is investing over CHF 325 million to expand its AI and cloud infrastructure in Switzerland, potentially aiming to mitigate the digital sovereignty concerns raised by the government.
